text:
Priya (Product): Quick sync — need to lock Q2 scope for the Optimize toolkit. We're debating four deliverables: 1) adaptive batching heuristics UI + backend, 2) prefix/KV cache visibility + cache invalidation primitives, 3) quantization recommendation flow (auto-suggest profiles), 4) eval-triggered regression alerts. Please react with P1/P2/P3 and call out hard constraints (SLOs, customer commitments, infra risk). Thanks!

Marco (Eng): P1 for adaptive batching (big immediate $ impact). P2 caching visibility. P3 quant recs. Alerts are nice-to-have but avoid P1 unless we define false-positive budget.

Dylan (ML): Agree with Marco. For quant recs we need model offline evals + a quick A/B harness. P2→P1 if we can get a 2-3 day offline job per model family. Also we should prioritize per-model-family profiles not one-size-fits-all.

Sana (PM): Customer asks: BetaCo and AtlasLegal asked for cache visibility + invalidation hooks. They say caching caused stale responses in one pilot. Marta, can you confirm severity from CS?

Marta (Customer Success): Confirmed — 1 BetaCo production incident last month, outage window ~3h due to stale prefix caching + tiled policy. They want cache TTL controls + a kill-switch. They rated this high (will block rollout). So cache invalidation is a hard constraint for those customers.

Priya (Product): Noted — so caching moves to P1 for customers with invalidation requirement, else P2. For batching, what's the SLO lift/latency trade we accept? Marco?

Marco (Eng): Target: 95th p90 increase <= 30ms for interactive routes when batching is enabled. If we can keep p99 under +120ms. We can implement adaptive batch size + tail-latency gating. Implementation estimate: 4 wks core + 1 wk rollout & canary.

Dylan (ML): For eval-triggered alerts we need: (a) define eval set, (b) threshold on delta of quality metrics (e.g., throughput BLEU-like or embedding drift), (c) backfill window. Low false positives => need baseline smoothing. Rough infra: 2 wks for hooks + 2 wks for evaluation service.

Sana (PM): Can we split roadmap into Phase A (must-have for customers + infra safety) and Phase B (econ/optimization features)? Proposal: Phase A = cache invalidation & TTL UI, batching basics (safe defaults + gating), rollout kill-switch. Phase B = quant recs + eval alerts + advanced batching heuristics.

Priya (Product): Proposal sounds reasonable. Any customer commitments that force shifting Phase B earlier?

Marta (Customer Success): AtlasLegal is interested in quantization recs (to reduce cost) but not blocking. BetaCo will block on cache controls only.

Marco (Eng): Implementation risks: quant recs require model benchmarking infra + per-arch kernel evaluation; high variance across families. Recommend prototype as experimental feature behind flag for 6 customers first.

Dylan (ML): Agree+note: We should capture per-workload quality regressions vs quant profile in our eval harness. Suggest storing per-prompt cohort metrics in eval DB for alerting.

Sana (PM): Launch criteria checklist draft:
- Phase A: cache invalidation + TTL UI behind feature flag, batching safe defaults, kill-switch, canary to 5 customers, runbooks + SLO dashboard.
- Phase B: quant recs proto + offline benchmarks, eval alert alpha for pilot customers, ops training.

Priya (Product): OK — action items:
- Marco: timeline & spike for adaptive batching gating (due EOD Thu)
- Marco & Dylan: feasibility spike for quant recs (2wk) — include infra cost estimate
- Marta: prioritize customer list for Phase A canary (today)
- Sana: update roadmap doc & ship acceptance criteria (tomorrow)

Marco (Eng): Ack — will post spike PR with perf numbers.

Dylan (ML): I'll draft eval metric list and smoothing strategy in a short doc.

Marta (Customer Success): I'll get BetaCo/AtlasLegal pushback notes and add to the canary risks doc.

deploy-bot: @priyaa Prod-incident-note created: incident-2026-03-cache-stale-beta — linked to BetaCo report (internal).

Priya (Product): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene Fri 11am for final scope sign-off. Please add any blockers in-thread before then. :thumbsup!
